summary: Arvin hunches over a weathered titanium manifold inside the sweltering hold of a converted fuel tanker. Beside him, Milo wipes grease onto a worn rag while staring at a digital pressure gauge that flickers red. The air is thick with the smell of kerosene and old copper. Arvin uses a magnifying loupe to inspect a hairline fracture near the fuel intake valve. Milo reaches out to tap the metal, feeling for the heat signature of the leak with his bare fingertips. "The metal is screaming under this much torque, Arvin."
settingText: Mobile Launch-Shop tanker interior — maintained retro-industrial aerospace workshop, painted metal, tactile analog-digital instruments, organized tools, practical task lighting and controlled localized wear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The metal is singing under the torque. Do you want another turn or a new bracket?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: That may be the first convincing argument you have made for staying anywhere.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: It is an argument for staying long enough to become part of one another's stories.

summary: Outside the tanker, Lucia stands on a ridge of sun-bleached sandstone, watching the horizon through heavy binoculars. Arvin climbs up to join her, his heavy leather boots crunching on the brittle desert crust. She shifts her weight, pointing toward a distant dust plume caused by an Tethergrid patrol unit. Lucia pulls a heavy, modified detonator from her utility belt and offers it to him with a sharp, expectant look. Arvin keeps his hands firmly at his sides, refusing to touch the militarized device. "I'm building a phone line for the thirsty, not a fuse for your war."
settingText: Mojave limestone ridge — pale fractured stone, bright high-desert sun, long sightlines, sparse scrub and the launch corridor below.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: We are giving Tetherwell's locked-out communities control of their pumps. If this network ever becomes a weapon, they decide—not us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: Was that you leaving a sentence human on purpose?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Yes. I am trying to make a habit of it.

summary: Cyrus sits inside the cockpit of a sleek, black interceptor vehicle, his eyes tracking Arvin on a glass display. He adjusts a manual dial, causing the engine to roar as he steers the massive machine over a jagged rock shelf. In the distance, Arvin scrambles to deploy a heavy camouflage netting over a silver tanker. Cyrus leans forward, his face illuminated by the amber glow of the console, and taps a physical kill-switch. "I can smell the kerosene and the desperation from ten miles out."
settingText: Tethergrid mobile interception platform — immaculate graphite corporate hardware, brushed alloy, tactile/glass controls, restrained cyan/amber status light, Mojave terrain beyond.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: Kerosene on the wind. They are tired, exposed, and still building. Adjust your assumptions.
